text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Friday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Lithuanian state justice organisations were shocked by a new law on pay as they say that due to inflation it means their wages will fall and qualified people will quit the law for the private sector.

- Zigmas Skirkevicius, a representative of the government of the northern Panevezhys region, resigned after police searched his appartment for fake police and customs seals but denied he was linked to any criminal activities.
- Prime Minister Mindaugas Stankevicius is expecting a reply from his Latvian counterpart Andris Shkele on proposals to solve their sea border dispute.
- The Lithuanian national soccer team performed well in their first game against world champions Brazil and were only beaten 3-1.

- If voters managed to meet the expectations of political parties at the elections on Sunday then parliament would need 280 seats instead of 141. The Homeland Union/Conservative Party expects to win 40-45 seats, the Democratic Labour Party 37-43, the Christian Democrats 20 and the Centre Union 19.
- Stankevicius said that from November 1 the monthly pension will be increased by 10 litas ($2.5) to 110 litas ($27.5).

- President Algirdas Brazauskas said in a speech to the Belgian parliament that the expansion of the EU should not be prevented by worries over its cost. He was certain the political and economic benefits would outweigh the financial burden.

- Three Russian military vessels dropped anchor near the Latvian border. Lithuanian sea frontier guards did not notice them although they had been informed by navy headquarters of their movement towards the Lithuanian border.

- The government has prepared a new program on investment for the period of 1997-1999 that includes 278 projects requiring 7.97 billion litas of investment or 5.7 times more than expected during 1995-97. Experts, having analyzed the failure of the previous program, doubt the viability of this new project.

- The only profitable airline in Lithuania, state-owned Lithuanian Airlines, is negotiating with Sweden's SAAB to lease one or two 35-seat planes for use on routes that are not in high demand such as to Warsaw, Berlin, Kiev, St Petersburg and Kaliningrad. During the first-half of 1996, the company made a 1.8 million litas profit and a turnover of 79 million litas.
